items.headline: Trump expects renewed Iran talks 'this week,' possibly as early as Monday, even as Iran's FM warns of readiness for 'doomsday war'
items.summary: In a Sunday Axios interview, Trump said he expects the US and Iran to hold more talks this week, with two regional sources saying another round of indirect talks via Qatari mediators could happen as soon as Monday 28 Sep. Hours earlier, Iranian FM Araghchi told state media Tehran is prepared for renewed fighting -- even a 'doomsday war' -- if talks fail, while stressing diplomacy remains on the table. Neither the 7-day Hormuz roadmap Trump rejected Saturday nor the underlying 24 Sep ultimatum has been formally withdrawn by either side.
items.actionable: Trump's talk-optimism is already pulling war premium out of Brent while WTI stays supply-risk-bid -- treat Monday's Asia open as a binary-headline day (talks-resume vs. doomsday-war rhetoric) rather than a clean directional bet on the silver/miner sleeve.

items.headline: Oil benchmarks diverge in weekend Globex trade: Brent -5.4% to $98.70 as talk-hope cuts war premium, WTI +1.3% to $93.58 on Hormuz supply risk
items.summary: Brent crude dropped below $100 to settle around $98.70 (-5.4%) as Trump's Sunday comments about resuming Iran talks eased the geopolitical risk premium, while WTI rose about 1.3% to $93.58 as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains essentially shut. The divergence reflects Brent's greater sensitivity to global-supply-restoration headlines versus WTI's closer link to the physical North American/Hormuz-linked barrel.
items.actionable: This corrects Saturday's 'oil spikes on rejection' framing -- Brent actually fell hard into the weekend close, so don't assume the war-premium tailwind for gold/silver miners is intact; WTI's firmness is the more reliable Hormuz-risk signal right now.

items.headline: Gold and silver climb in weekend trade to $4,294.40 and $64.18, reversing Friday's dip
items.summary: Gold rebounded to roughly $4,294.40/oz and silver to about $64.18/oz over the weekend Globex session, both above Friday's softer cash close ($4,265 gold, ~$63.5 silver) when a firmer dollar and 5.18% 10-year real yields had weighed on the metals. The bounce lines up with the mixed Iran headlines (talk-optimism vs. 'doomsday war' rhetoric) rather than a clean yield or dollar move.
items.actionable: The levered silver/gold-miner book is opening Monday from a firmer weekend base than Friday's print, but the move is headline-driven and could reverse fast if Monday's Iran talks headline turns unambiguously de-escalatory.

items.headline: Strait of Hormuz traffic still near total shutdown seven months into the crisis; war-risk insurance ~40x pre-crisis levels
items.summary: Commercial transits through Hormuz remain in the single digits a day versus roughly 85/day pre-crisis, with reports of as few as 1 ship transiting on some September days. War-risk insurance for tankers is now priced at roughly 40 times pre-crisis levels and six Protection & Indemnity clubs have withdrawn coverage entirely, seven months after the crisis began in late February 2026.
items.actionable: The physical chokepoint disruption is structurally unresolved regardless of this weekend's talk headlines -- keeps the inflation-hedge/oil-shock case for the gold-silver miner sleeve intact even if Brent's headline-driven premium fades.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds near $84,265 after 44% Q3 rally; spot ETFs pull in $2.39bn weekly inflow
items.summary: Bitcoin was trading around $84,265-$84,830 on Sunday, consolidating after a roughly 44% rally in Q3 2026 and a volatility squeeze into quarter-end. US spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted about $2.39bn in net inflows for the week ended 25 September, including a single-day $999m inflow on Monday 21 Sep -- the largest daily total of 2026.
items.actionable: Crypto (the only 24/7 market) is holding its weekend gains rather than rolling over on the Iran 'doomsday war' rhetoric, a modestly reassuring risk-appetite signal ahead of Monday's Asia/HK-tech open.

items.headline: Hang Seng slips 1% Friday; mainland China reopens Monday for only three sessions before Golden Week shutdown
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index closed down 1.01% at 24,510.09 and the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.13% to 4,311.78 on Friday in holiday-thin trade, with Xiaomi (-2.6%) and NetEase (-3.1%) among the laggards. Mainland Shanghai/Shenzhen markets, closed since 25 Sep for Mid-Autumn Festival, reopen Monday 28 Sep but will only trade three sessions (Mon-Wed) before shutting again for the week-long National Day Golden Week holiday (1-7 Oct).
items.actionable: A truncated three-day mainland trading window before Golden Week, layered on weak Friday follow-through and the Iran binary risk, argues for staying selective rather than adding broad beta to 0700/0981/1810 into Monday's reopen.

items.headline: MAS stress-tests listed companies against a severe AI-downturn scenario; SGX RegCo unveils new issuer disclosure rules
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore ran stress tests on SGX-listed companies against a severe artificial-intelligence-driven market downturn scenario, while SGX RegCo separately announced new disclosure rules aimed at building a stronger value-creation culture among issuers. Both moves come in the same week Jefferies initiated Buy ratings on DBS and UOB (Hold on OCBC), citing rising SORA and improving net interest margins.
items.actionable: Regulatory scrutiny of an AI-bubble tail-risk scenario is a reminder that the Singapore bank leg, while a beneficiary of higher SORA, is not immune to a global AI-driven risk-off shock -- keep sizing disciplined even after the fresh Jefferies Buy calls.

items.headline: US-China critical-minerals talks end without a deal; China's rare-earth export-control pause nears 10 November expiry
items.summary: Bessent and Greer's meetings with Vice Premier He Lifeng around the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit concluded without a public deal on rare-earth magnet flows, and a US official said China's mineral-flow restoration remains below expectations. China's 12-month suspension of its expanded rare-earth export controls is now set to expire 10 November 2026, just six weeks away, with no indication yet of an extension.
items.actionable: The approaching 10 Nov export-control cliff, on top of still-underperforming magnet flows, keeps the structural case for the rare-earth watchlist (MP, Lynas, USA Rare Earth) intact and argues for watching for headlines on an extension or lapse as the date nears.

items.headline: Houthis strike Saudi Aramco's Yanbu hub and a Riyadh target; six missiles intercepted
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on a target in Riyadh and Aramco facilities at the Red Sea port of Yanbu on 25 September; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted six ballistic missiles, with no confirmed damage or casualties. Aramco supplies roughly 10% of global oil demand.
items.actionable: Continued Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure add a second, independent supply-risk vector alongside Hormuz, reinforcing the oil-shock/inflation-hedge case for the gold-silver miners leg.

items.headline: BofA Flow Show: global equity funds swing to outflow as US leads the reversal
items.summary: BofA's weekly Flow Show (week ended 23 Sep 2026) showed US equity funds losing $21.1bn and global equity funds losing a net $10.2bn -- a sharp reversal from the prior week's +$63.8bn US equity inflow (the best week in three months). Fixed income kept its 74-week inflow streak alive (+$17.3bn); the Bull & Bear Indicator eased to 9.3, still in the contrarian 'Sell' zone.
items.actionable: A one-week swing from the best equity-inflow week in three months to an outright outflow is an early tell that positioning is reacting to the hawkish Fed -- a reason not to read Friday's index rally as confirmation the flow backdrop has turned durably risk-on.

items.headline: Wall Street closes hawkish week with a rally as 10-year yield hits post-2008 high
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow gained 0.93% to 51,828.62 (snapping a three-week losing streak), and the Nasdaq added ~0.48% to 27,068.72 on Friday, with all three posting weekly gains despite the 10-year Treasury yield climbing to 5.18%, its highest since the 2008 financial crisis. VIX eased to ~14.9 even as the bond selloff continued.
items.actionable: Equities shrugging off 5%+ yields is a near-term risk-on tell, but with the weekend's mixed Iran signals on top, the yield/geopolitics combination still favors keeping the cash pile large rather than chasing the rally.

items.headline: Week ahead: August PCE due Wednesday, September payrolls Friday with consensus roughly halving to ~85k
items.summary: The week of 28 Sep-2 Oct brings Dallas Fed manufacturing Monday, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge (August core PCE, running near 3.3% y/y) on Wednesday 30 Sep, Q2 GDP final and jobless claims mid-week, ISM Manufacturing PMI Thursday, and September nonfarm payrolls Friday 2 Oct with consensus around 85k, roughly half August's 162k. Around 22 Fed speaking engagements are scheduled, keeping policy risk elevated after September's 25bp hike and signal of at least one more increase.
items.actionable: Friday's payrolls print is the key swing factor for whether the Fed's hawkish path holds -- a soft number would cut against the 'further hikes' narrative embedded in the model's bond calls, while a hot core-PCE print Wednesday could pressure the silver/miner sleeve via real yields.

note: Pre-Asia-open Monday run, 28 Sep 2026 ~07:0x SGT -- as of the Friday US close carried into the weekend Globex reopen; SGX (09:00 SGT) and HKEX (09:30 SGT) have not yet opened. Explicitly swept Sat 26 and Sun 27 Sep: the dominant new thread is that Trump told Axios on Sunday he expects renewed Iran talks this week (possibly Monday), even as Iran's FM warned of readiness for a 'doomsday war' -- a materially more current and more two-sided picture than Saturday's flat rejection headline. Using the authoritative closes provided (SI=F $64.18, GC=F $4294.40, BZ=F $98.70 -5.4%, CL=F $93.58 +1.3%, BTC-USD ~$84,265), the actual weekend move was Brent falling hard (talk-optimism) while WTI and precious metals firmed (Hormuz supply risk intact) -- this corrects the prior run's 'oil spikes bullish' framing, which is superseded. 5 of the 13 items above (27/27/27/26/27 Sep) are within the last 24-48 hours, meeting the freshness requirement; Congress/insider filings and fresh Monday-morning Asia/SG corporate announcements were checked but none had posted yet ahead of the exchange opens.
